summary: Crotched Mountain's state lookout dates to 1915; the tower and warden's cabin are gone and communication towers now stand on the summit.

facts.design: Open-top wooden tower about 20 ft high with a small cabin; later a 45-ft steel tower with a two-room cabin
facts.status_note: Tower and warden's cabin are gone; communication towers and buildings now stand on the summit. Removal date not found in the sources read.

events.note: New lookout station in the 1915-1916 biennium; the first station was open-top wood, about 20 ft.
Portsmouth Herald says it was abandoned in 1921; the 1921 state report calls it an emergency station that year.
Listed among five stations temporarily or permanently discontinued that year.
Peterborough Transcript note: a new 45-foot steel tower replaces the one abandoned in 1921. Conflicts with the 1930 Herald item.
Portsmouth Herald item dated January 3, 1930 describes the reopening with a 45-foot steel tower and a two-room cabin.
Photo caption: a person sitting on the roof of the fire warden's cabin at the lookout tower.

evidence.supports: Summit is in the town of Francestown
evidence.quote: The 2,063-foot (629 m) summit of the mountain is in the town of Francestown
1915-1916 biennium: A new lookout station was constructed.

evidence.supports: First station: open-top wood, about 20 ft, small cabin, opened 1915
evidence.quote: Crotched Mountain station was opened in 1915 with an open top town of wood, 20 feet high, and a small cabin.
This included the Crotchet station in Francestown, which was an emergency station..

In 1922 five of the 29 stations were either temporarily or permanently discontinued because it was believed that the service from them did not justify the expense of their maintenance, except in emergency.

evidence.supports: 1925 steel tower replaces the one abandoned in 1921
evidence.quote: A new 45-foot steel lookout tower on Crotched Mountain replaces the one abandoned in 1921.

evidence.supports: 1930 reopening with 45-foot steel tower and two-room cabin
evidence.quote: In 1921 it was abandoned, but was reopened this year, when a 45-foot steel tower and a two room cabin were built.

evidence.supports: Agency is the New Hampshire Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: New Hampshire - Hillsborough County - New Hampshire Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Photo of a person on the warden's cabin roof at the tower, 1943
evidence.quote: Sept. 14, 1943, sitting on top of the roof of the fire warden’s cabin at the fire lookout tower on top of Crotched Mountain.

evidence.supports: Climbing the steps into the cabin on top was popular, per the article (a general statement, not the writer's own memory)
evidence.quote: It was very popular to climb up the mountain and then up the steps of the tower into the cabin on top to take in the view.

evidence.supports: Woods road almost to the top before the ski area; writer calls the tower Forest Service
evidence.quote: Before there was a ski area, there was just a woods road almost to the top, where a Forest Service Fire Lookout Tower stood.

evidence.supports: Tower and warden's cabin gone; communication towers and buildings on the summit
evidence.quote: Gone are the Fire Lookout Tower and Warden’s cabin, replaced by communication towers and buildings.

evidence.supports: Ski area on the northern slopes today
evidence.quote: The Crotched Mountain Ski & Ride occupies the northern slopes of the mountain.

evidence.supports: Rehabilitation center on the southern ridge in Greenfield
evidence.quote: The Crotched Mountain Rehabilitation Center occupies a portion of the mountain's southern ridge in Greenfield.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Peterborough Transcript note quoted on the Forest Lookouts page dates the 45-foot steel tower to 1925. A Portsmouth Herald item dated January 3, 1930 describes a reopening with a 45-foot steel tower and two-room cabin. The story gives both and does not choose.

The Forest Lookouts page and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list name the New Hampshire Forestry Commission. The Ledger-Transcript calls it a Forest Service tower. The story uses the state listing and notes the difference.
The Portsmouth Herald says it was abandoned in 1921. The 1921-22 state report calls the Crotched station an emergency station in 1921 and lists it among stations discontinued in 1922.

sources.title: Mountain of Memories: Early skiing and vision for Crotched Mountain

notes_for_editor: Removal date not found. The Francestown Heritage Museum February 2022 newsletter (search snippet says the tower is listed as no longer standing in Tower Quest) returned 404 from the cache and was not used. The NH Division of Forests PDF and fire-tower page returned 403. A 1926 Facebook photo caption (snippet only) describes a wooden tower, which conflicts with the 1925 steel tower; it was not fetched or cited. The brief's height_m 13.7 matches the 45-foot steel tower.
